question.leadin: This period of less than ten years caused its country's population to drop by nearly twenty percent.
question.text: Name this period of disease and starvation caused by infected plants that affected a constituent country of the United Kingdom from 1845 to 1852.
question.answerHtml: Irish Potato Famine (or Great Famine ; or Great Hunger ; accept Gorta Mor )
question.clue: Protestant schools engaging in "Souperism" during this event caused friction with the local population.

swap.leadin: Eamon de Valera founded this nation's largest political party, Fianna Fail.
swap.text: Name this nation, with capital at Dublin. Its northern neighbor is still part of the United Kingdom.
swap.clue: Leaders from this country include Eamon de Valera and Patrick Pearse.

question.text: Gladstone unsuccessfully pushed for the home rule of this country first conquered by Henry VIII. The failed Easter Rising occurred in this nation, which was also home to the Battle of the Boyne.
question.clue: The Cranborne Report described the collaboration of this neutral nation with the Allies.

swap.leadin: This party's name means "Ours Alone" or "We Ourselves."
swap.text: Name this political party, which does not sit in the British Parliament, founded by Arthur Griffith. This Irish Republican political party was once led by Gerry Adams as well as former IRA leader Martin McGuinness.
swap.clue: Former Tanaiste Eamon Gilmore was originally a member of this party before eventually joining the Labour Party.

question.text: One of the highlights of Paisley's leadership in Northern Ireland was taking part in negotiations for this 1998 treaty. This treaty, which is named for a Christian holiday, ended the violent period known as "The Troubles."
question.answerHtml: Good Friday Agreement [accept, but do NOT reveal Belfast Agreement]
question.clue: Bertie Ahern and David Andrews were signatories of this document, which was primarily negotiated by David Trimble and John Hume.

swap.leadin: Douglas Hyde and Patrick Pearse were members of a League founded in 1893 to promote a language known by this term.
swap.text: Name this cultural term, which underwent a "revival" in the late 1800s that opposed English influence in Ireland. This term refers to Irish and Scottish culture before English invasions.
swap.clue: This cultural term, which underwent a "revival" in the late 1800s that opposed English influence in Ireland. This term refers to Irish and Scottish culture before English invasions.

question.leadin: The Fianna ("fi-na") was a major supporter of this rebellion.
question.text: Name this 1916 anti-British rebellion organized by the IRB which began on a namesake holiday and was centered at the General Post Office. It was defeated by 16,000 British soldiers after a week.
question.answerHtml: Easter Rising [or Easter Rebellion; accept Éiri Amach na Cásca; prompt on partial]
question.clue: That participant, Patrick Pearse, was part of a group that took over locations such as Boland's Bakery and Jacob's Biscuit Factory, though it was centered in the General Post Office.

swap.text: For his role in the War of Independence, Collins was appointed Minister of Finance by this Taoiseach. This man founded Fianna Fail and was later elected as the third president of Ireland.
swap.clue: This leader's American citizenship allowed him to escape execution after the Easter Rising.

question.text: Forgeries falsely implicated this Irish Nationalist politician in the murders, leading to the downfall of his coalition with the Liberal party. His political career was ultimately undone by his affair with Kitty O'Shea.
question.clue: This supporter of the Cumbrian farmers and critic of the Chelsea Barracks development plan had some of his correspondence published after a Freedom of Information request by journalists at The Guardian.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a historical event.
swap.text: This former school teacher and barrister served as one of the commanders of the Easter Rising. He was declared President of the Provisional Government and executed after the British retook Dublin.
swap.clue: This man praised war for warming the "heart of the earth" with the "red wine of battlefields," a metaphor reflecting his mystical belief in "blood sacrifice."

question.text: Following the Glorious Revolution, William decisively defeated his predecessor, James II, at this battle in Ireland, fought at a namesake river.
question.clue: Commemorated by a contemporary holiday called The Twelfth, this battle was followed a year later by the loser's successful defense of Limerick.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about James II's attempts to regain the English throne.
swap.text: 1. points) More decisive than the Boyne was this July 12, 1691 battle in which Ginkel crushed the Jacobites after their retreat to Ireland.

question.leadin: Daisen Kofun, the largest example of one of these structures in Japan, is shaped like a key-hole.
question.text: Name these structures exemplified by Newgrange in Ireland. In the UK, these structures are known as barrows.
question.answerHtml: burial mounds [accept passage grave or passage tombs; accept tumuli or tumulus; accept BUT DO NOT OTHERWISE REVEAL kurgans]
question.clue: The largest "platform" example of these structures in North America is the "Monks" one in Illinois.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about illuminated manuscripts.
swap.text: A masterpiece of the Hiberno-Saxon style, this manuscript, begun in the late 8th century, was moved from the Isle of Iona to the monastery that gives it its name. It is also sometimes known as the Book of Columba.
swap.clue: This illuminated Irish manuscript was a compilation of parts of the Vulgate and the Vetus Latina. It is especially known for its illustrations.

question.leadin: "'God save Ireland!' said the heroes / 'God save Ireland' said they all." Answer the following about Irish rebel music.
question.text: Dominic Behan's song "Come Out Ye [these people]" asks them to tell their wives "...how the IRA made you run like hell away / from the green and lovely lanes of Killeshandra." This notoriously brutal auxiliary force opened fire at a Gaelic football match at Croke Park.
question.clue: Lyrics by Dominic Behan invite these people to "show your wives how you won medals down in Flanders."

swap.leadin: The Volunteer Force named for this province, led by Frederick Crawford, purchased arms from the Germans to defend itself during the Howth gunrunning scandal.
swap.text: Name this province that signed a namesake covenant in 1912 to oppose Home Rule, which its Unionist Party led by Edward Carson referred to as "Rome Rule."
swap.clue: This province was the site of an early 17th century "plantation," in which James I settled thousands of Scots here.

question.text: This younger sister of Charles Parnell led the Ladies' Land League and wrote The Tale of a Great Sham. A plaque on her tombstone carries her quote "the best part of independence; the independence of mind."
question.answerHtml: Anna Catherine Parnell [grudgingly prompt on (A.) Parnell ]

swap.text: Chavez came up with the Obama-inspiring slogan "Si, se puede" while participating in one of these events in Phoenix in 1972.
swap.clue: An Act of Parliament designed to counter this action was euphemistically titled the Prisoners (Temporary Discharge for Ill-Health) Act 1913, but became better known as the Cat and Mouse Act.

question.leadin: Name these sources which document the extreme weather events of 535 to 536 C.E., the most significant global cooling in the past 2,000 years.
question.text: This set of annals documents the frigid weather of the 530s as well as many other severe climate events over centuries of Irish history. These annals were compiled by monks on a namesake island in the Lakes of Killarney.

swap.leadin: This man wrote the autobiography One Day in My Life, and his writings are anthologized in Skylark Sing Your Lonely Song.
swap.text: Name this member of the IRA elected to the British parliament while in prison. He died in 1981 after engaging in a protracted hunger strike to protest prison policies and the classification of IRA members as criminals.
swap.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.
